title: Lovely Meeting
subtitle: With a shake of her head, the little white duck finds the goldcrest.

items.text: The Star
Lovely Meeting
SPDM Library

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Wow! So this is the library in Vertin's school!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: So many people here! Hmm, they're probably around my age.
A gorgeous sap-green dress jumps into the library of SPDM. Its owner keeps talking in a sing-song tone, like a chirping goldcrest.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Heh heh, we've also got this many shelves in the library of Sotheby's Manor!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Are there any alchemy workshops and potion warehouses here, like in our manor?
The young lady stands on tiptoe, looking around this place curiously.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Where can I find Ms. Bouanich? Madam Z told me to come here, but she didn't give any other clues.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: *sighs* The people here really need Mr. Teakettler, who is always nice and warm to the guests. Just twist his teapot ear, then he can take you anywhere.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: If not so, placing a Luck-A-Day Potion at the entrance would help as well.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: If I had made it before I came, Ms. Bouanich and I might have met by now. Or she will just pop up behind me!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Are you looking for me?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh, my word!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oops, that was too loud. Where are my manners!
Sotheby straightens the wrinkles on her dress and gives out her hand like a real lady.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Nice to meet you! Are you Ms. Bouanich?
The other girl nods haughtily. Her uniform speaks for herself.
It seems to be a historic "first meeting" for them.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: That's fantastic. How did you find me? Did you see me in the Oneiromancy? Or through a crystal orb?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Either way, it is the great arcanum ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hah! I'm much greater than that. Look at you, dressed as if you'd just been to a ball. You are as eye-catching as … the pigment poured on a sketch!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I saw you the moment I came into the library!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: A ball? Ha! Does the Foundation hold balls, too?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: No, I'm saying ... Hmm, does every friend of Vertin's talk this way?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Never mind. Madam Z told me you wanted to look up the materials on "the mysterious school that believes in numbers" here.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: That's right! Ms. Moissan told me she will thoroughly check the documents in the Foundation archive, so I'll go through the books in the SPDM library!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: If we can find anything about that school, we can be of more help to Vertin and her team!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Sotheby, but I'm afraid this situation is going to disappoint you.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: While you spent the last hour looking for Teakettler's ear, the kindhearted monitor assistant already gained the valuable access to the library. But I haven't found any records regarding "the mysterious school that believes in numbers" yet.
Like a bolt out of the blue.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh! But, but Ms. Moissan said, there are soooo many books here that they can cover the entire back of a Stronsay Beast!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: That's a bit exaggerated, but, ahem, she's right!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Nevertheless, the librarian was transferred to a more important position years ago due to the "Storm."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Many old books are not yet sorted. Some even went missing in the chaos.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: The only relevant materials I could find are the stories of Pythagoras and some books on mathematical theorems, but I don't think they have anything to do with Vertin's issue.
What Matilda sees now is a pair of tear-dimmed eyes.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: That means ... I can't do anything to help them?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Please stop being emotional. It doesn't work on this professional member of the Foundation!
She looks away and clears her throat like a grown-up.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ahem! Without field investigation permission, I can't take you out to collect information.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: But in fact, there is still another reference room only known to the most outstanding monitor assistant.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hooray!
Other students in the library cast disgruntled glances at them.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Shh, shh! It's a violation to make noises in the library! Please follow me, Ms. Sotheby!
Tall shelves.
Unfamiliar surroundings.
An impossible mission.
The girls walk through the shelves like fish swimming through coral.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Thank you so much, Ms. Bouanich.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: You mentioned "ball." I haven't heard that word for a very long time.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I remember what Mr. Karson, my butler, had taught me. He said, "Express your gratitude to fair ladies by holding a grand ball."

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I'll write to my father and ask for a brand-new, unsinkable, and maneuverable rock 'n' roll park. I'm sure he will gladly say yes.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Maneuverable rock 'n' roll park?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Yes! We can hold a twist ball on it when Vertin and her team are back!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Please allow me to say NO! The monitor assistant of SPDM will never participate in such an inelegant activity.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Wait. Did you just say Vertin and "her team"?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ahem, we can talk about the ball later.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: The kindhearted Matilda Bouanich will try her best to help you with the task. But o-of course, it's only out of her sense of responsibility, not for some personal reasons.
They go faster and faster.
Finally, they reach their destination.
"Unnecessary Information" Room
To patch the fragmented eras in the future ...
And to store the currently unimportant files and reports ...
People built this reference room in the shape of a box with gray and white walls.
During this awful time, which might last for ages, people call it—
The footnote of history.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Here we are: the reference room storing "unnecessary information." It's a place ignored by most staff.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Even so, this careful, reliable monitor assistant will not let go of any details.
She knocks on the rusty sign haughtily.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I hereby officially appoint you as the chief assistant of monitor assistant of SPDM! I will take my responsibility and teach you how to become a devoted Foundation member!
Matilda pulls off the cloth covering the archive cabinet.
Dust rises in the air.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Here is your first task: read through these unsorted, old files, all of them.
The monitor assistant takes a dusty file from the cabinet. The paper inside has already turned yellow.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I have searched all the archived ones. These are the last parts.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Most of them are discarded administrative documents, low-priority materials, and substandard reports written by rookie investigators.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: By the way, you should know I didn't sort any of them out for you, and they don't necessarily have what you want!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: It's alright! Leave them to me! I love reading!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Humph! You'd better do.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Here's the key. Keep it safe. You can sit on the cushion there when you sort out the files. I-I don't want your dress to stain the stone bench.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I'll go see if I missed any files. Listen! This monitor assistant will test you on your familiarity with these files when she's back!
Three Hours Later

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Double check completed. Looks like I didn't miss any relevant files.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Phew! Quite a long day.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I doubt if that spoiled lady can finish all the materials. She must have been bored and fallen asleep, waiting for her Teakettler in the dream ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: It takes much more than dancing at balls to be a Foundation investigator.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I'll send her back to that teacher when she wakes up.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: In the end, it will be the kindhearted Matilda who finishes the task for her. Being a great monitor assistant comes with great responsibility!
Again, Matilda gently pushes the door open.
Surprisingly, she is welcomed with an energetic greeting.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh, Ms. Bouanich!
Standing on a ladder, Sotheby gives her a big smile with a stack of files in her hand.
The files she didn't finish reading are scattered on the ground, while the others have been well organized in the cabinet.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: You ... You didn't fall asleep? Did you sort out these files?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hmm? Yes! And I love these books in uncommon shapes! There are so many wonderful stories!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I often read books with Sasana when Father wasn't at home. We read and read until the Redcomb Aves woke up the sun. Moreover, these files are much easier than Ms. Moissan's reading task.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Here, the gentleman from River Conwy tamed a whole group of Afancs! How marvellous is that!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Oh, okay. Looks like you meet the basic requirements for being a rookie investigator!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I-I guess you are qualified to be my chief assistant.
The young lady doesn't pay much attention to the mumbles from the monitor assistant.
She is busy announcing her big discovery.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: And I also found this interesting report! It tells a lot about the "Storm" and the "numbers."

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh! Will this be helpful to Vertin?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hmm? Show it to me.
She takes a pile of yellowed paper from Sotheby.
This neat and orderly written report has no beginning or end.
Obviously, the author is a meticulous person.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "… I have to say, it is undoubtedly a violation to submit such a report, but it will be a travesty of the truth and human sense if I cover it up."

items.speaker: Matilda & Writer of the Report
items.text: Peace, sense, justice—they have always been the creeds in my heart, and are now the reason why I have decided to write down the whole thing.

items.speaker: Writer of the Report
items.text: A long time has passed since the first attack of the most severe crisis in our time. But we are still wondering, what on earth does it mean?

items.speaker: Writer of the Report
items.text: That was the eve of the millennium, of which no one had any memories, illogically. The next day, time was already reversed to 1996 the moment we opened our eyes.

items.speaker: Writer of the Report
items.text: We walked out of the building made of gray and white marble as usual, hardly aware that the sun we bathed in was from another time.

items.speaker: Writer of the Report
items.text: Our survival was unexpected and almost unbelievable in such a calamity which swept the globe.

items.speaker: Writer of the Report
items.text: Why did the headquarters of the Foundation survive the reverse? Why couldn't we find our younger selves in the outside world? Did any other regions survive it as we did? What was the cause behind this calamity?

items.speaker: Writer of the Report
items.text: I didn't know, nor did anyone else.

items.speaker: Writer of the Report
items.text: Things remained unclear until time was reversed again. This time, we all witnessed that rain in the '80s.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Are these files Vertin needs?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I, I think so.
She says in a trembling voice.
This monitor assistant, who always claims to have a cool head, has never panicked so much.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: It's a report written by someone who witnessed the "Storm"!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: And it has recorded the "Storms" before Vertin became the Timekeeper?!
TO BE CONTINUED…
